key_insight: TurboVLA replaces the usual LLM-heavy vision-language-action pipeline with a direct vision+language-to-action mapping, cutting compute and memory dramatically. It achieves real-time robot control at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 using less than 1 GB of VRAM.
problem_solved: Traditional VLA systems rely on an LLM-centric V→L→A pipeline, which is slow and memory-intensive at every decision step. This makes real-time robotic control difficult on practical hardware.
method: Reformulates the VLA policy as a direct V+L→A mapping instead of routing through a large language model.
Reduces inference overhead by avoiding repeated LLM-style computation and intermediate representations.
Targets efficient deployment for real-time control on consumer-grade GPUs with minimal VRAM usage.
impact: This work makes VLA models far more practical for robotics and embodied AI by enabling fast, memory-efficient inference on a single RTX 4090. For practitioners, it suggests a path toward deployable real-time policies without requiring large accelerator clusters or excessive model compression.

paper_title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
paper_authors: Hengyi Xie, Chenfei Yao, Xianjin Wu, Xuanyang Xi, Yiping Tang
